summary: All three phases delivered their stated objectives. Phase-01 adds the CommitFailed pause path (running+passed → interrupted+passed) and phase-02 adds the corresponding resume path (detecting a passed+interrupted phase and re-running commit/handoff/cleanup without re-invoking the agent). Phase-03 adds the CleanupFailed pause path (running+committed|cleaning_up → interrupted+cleaning_up) and its resume path (skipping agent, gate, commit, and handoff). Commit subjects match the plan exactly. Two recurring unplanned-file edits (src/domain/errors.ts and src/app/resumeInstructions.ts) appear in phases 01 and 03 and are justified in both handoffs as following established project patterns. Two undisclosed deviations are present: the CommitFailed matrix column uses 'Unexpected' for the rate_limited run state rather than the plan's specified 'Stale', and the cleanupPhase catch uses Effect.catchAll rather than the plan's specified Effect.catchIf. Neither undermines correctness or the cross-phase boundary contracts.

attentionPoints: CommitFailed × rate_limited matrix disposition (phase-01): plan specifies 'Stale' but implementation uses 'Unexpected'. Semantically defensible (CommitFailed cannot arrive during a rate-limited run) but undisclosed in the phase-01 handoff — confirm intent.

Effect.catchAll on cleanupPhase (phase-03): plan specified Effect.catchIf scoped to the cleanup step's own error types. Implementation used Effect.catchAll. Locally scoped so risk is low, but broader than specified and not disclosed in the phase-03 handoff — confirm intent.

Confirm via code review.
